qt: to the Commission Giuseppe Antoci (The Left) Subject:

Through cohesion policy, the Recovery and Resilience Facility and other financial instruments, the European Union supports action to improve water infrastructure, reduce network losses and boost network resilience. In several Member States, including Italy, some of these investments involve concessionaires of the integrated water service, who are called upon to implement investment programmes financed, in whole or in part, with EU resources. In light of the principles of transparency, sound financial management and protection of the EU’s financial interests, it is essential to ensure that those resources produce verifiable results and are used in compliance with the obligations under the funding programmes. In view of the above, can the Commission answer the following: 1.

In the context of the EU-financed programmes, have audits or checks been carried out on the actual implementation of the co-financed investments and on compliance with the obligations under the programmes?

Does it use or intend to develop common indicators at EU level to assess the effectiveness of co-financed investments, with particular reference to reduction of network losses, to service quality and to infrastructure resilience?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (29.10.2026) Under shared management, Member States have the primary responsibility for the control and audit of projects supported by cohesion policy funds (including those related to water infrastructure) and their compliance with applicable rules. To exercise its supervisory role, the Commission assesses the functioning of the established national management and control systems through its own audits. 442 such audits covering cohesion policy funds have been carried out by the Commission since 2021, out of which 55 in Italy. As regards the Recovery and Resilience Facility implemented in direct management, the Commission carries out ex ante assessments on the satisfactory fulfilment of milestones and targets to ensure the legality and regularity of payments. These ex ante controls are complemented by risk-based ex post audits. End September 2026, 74 ex post audits have been carried out, and each national control system to prevent, detect and correct fraud, corruption, conflicts of interest and double funding has been audited at least once. The Commission uses common output and result indicators1 to monitor cohesion policy achievements, including those contributing to the improvement of water service quality, infrastructure resilience and the reduction in network losses. These achievements are published on the Cohesion Open Data Platform2. The proposed Performance Regulation3 will establish, for the 2028-2034 Multiannual Financial Framework, a harmonised set of performance indicators applicable to all EU budget programmes, which, among others, also cover investments in water infrastructure.
1 COMMISSION STAFF WORKING DOCUMENT Performance, monitoring and evaluation of the European

Regional Development Fund, the Cohesion Fund and the Just Transition Fund in 2021-2027; https://ec.europa.eu/regional_policy/sources/evaluation/performance2127/SWD_2025_346_SWD_PME_20212027.pdf. 2 https://cohesiondata.ec.europa.eu/. 3 https://commission.europa.eu/publications/budget-expenditure-tracking-and-performance-framework_en.
